newsitem.title: LEBANON: ISRAELI PLANES STRIKE AGAIN IN SOUTH LEBANON.
newsitem.headline: ISRAELI PLANES STRIKE AGAIN IN SOUTH LEBANON.

text.p: Israeli planes twice rocketed suspected Hizbollah guerrilla targets in south Lebanon on Sunday, security sources said.
Two Israeli warplanes fired a total of four rockets into the Wadi al-Qaysiyyeh valley north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, they said.
The air assault was followed by a heavy exchange of fire between the Moslem guerrillas and Israeli forces.
Hizbollah said one fighter was killed in "Sunday's military operations". It was not clear whether he was killed in the air raids or in Israeli artillery shelling.
In an earlier raid, planes rocketed the hills of Jabal Safi and Mleeta on the Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridge.
The two attacks brought to 38 the number of air raids into Lebanon in 1997.

Hizbollah in Beirut said shortly before the second air raid its guerrillas had targeted with "adequate weapons" a group of Israeli officers on the road leading to the outpost of Marqaba inside the Israeli security zone -- facing the Wadi al-Qayssiyyeh area.
Pro-Israeli militia sources in the zone said two mortar bombs hit an area near the outpost of Marqaba. Noone was injured in the attack, they said.

Earlier on Sunday, Hizbollah guerrillas attacked another Israeli outpost with machineguns and rocket-propelled grenades, the sources said. There were no casualties in the attack on the Sojoud outpost.
Shortly before the first air strike, residents of the south Lebanon village of Arnoun said Israeli forces advanced into their area and arrested six Lebanese civilians.
In Jerusalem, an Israeli army spokesman confirmed the operation and said all civilians were released.

"An Israeli force that was on operations in the area of Arnoun village in the eastern sector of the security zone...arrested three Hizbollah activists who participated in attacks against army forces in the security zone," he said.
"Lebanese civilians who were arrested during the same operation were released after clarification that they were not involved in hostile activities," the spokesman added.
The operation lasted less than two hours, according to residents who arrived in the nearby village of Kfar Tibnit in south Lebanon's central sector.
Israel occupies a 15-km-wide zone in south Lebanon. Moslem guerrillas attack Israeli and its allied forces in a bid to oust them from the area.
